title: Silver Lake, Intel-Backed Altera Confidentially Files for U.S. IPO
author: L
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Altera has confidentially submitted paperwork for a U.S. initial public offering, positioning the programmable-chip maker to capitalize on strong investor demand for semiconductor and artificial-intelligence businesses.

The San Jose, California-based company said its parent submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 to the Securities and Exchange Commission. The number of shares to be offered and the expected price range have not yet been determined. A confidential filing allows the company to begin the SEC review process without immediately disclosing detailed financial information.

Altera develops field-programmable gate arrays, or FPGAs, chips that customers can configure after manufacturing for specialized tasks. Its products are used in data centers, telecommunications networks, industrial machinery, AI systems, and aerospace and defense applications.

The company is controlled by technology-focused private-equity firm Silver Lake, which acquired a 51% stake from Intel in 2025 for $4.46 billion. That transaction valued Altera at $8.75 billion and restored the business as an independent company. Intel, which bought Altera for roughly $16.7 billion in 2015, continues to own the remaining 49%.

Reuters previously reported that the offering could raise more than $2 billion and take place as early as this year, although its timing and size remain subject to market conditions. If completed at that scale, the flotation would rank among the largest semiconductor IPOs in recent years.

The filing comes as the U.S. listings market regains momentum and investors continue to favor companies tied to expanding AI infrastructure. Altera Chief Executive Raghib Hussain said in July that the company expected revenue growth in the mid-20% range this year.

An IPO would give Altera fresh capital and provide Silver Lake and Intel with a potential route to monetize their holdings. However, the confidential submission does not guarantee that an offering will proceed or occur on any particular timetable, Altera cautioned.

Sources: Reuters and Intel
